scope: targeted correction set from the site owner's five rulings - not a full fact-check
summary: Thirty edits apply the owner's five rulings across lessons 7, 9, 10, 13 and 16. Lesson 9's Armada timeline moves from New Style to Old Style so it matches lesson 16 (sighted 19 July, fireships 27-28 July, Gravelines 29 July; Julian runs ten days behind Gregorian in 1588, checked against the New Style dates in Wikipedia's Spanish Armada article). The ships-returned figure becomes about two-thirds, around 65 to 67 of about 130, in both lesson 9 and lesson 16, and the lesson 9 knowledge check is re-keyed from 80 to 65. Essex's ages move to a 10 November 1565 birth: court at 19, Privy Council at 27, Cadiz at 30. The 1563 poor-relief powers are renamed the Act for the Relief of the Poor. Two stale mark schemes in lesson 7 still said Parker expelled ministers or expelled 30; both now say he suspended 37. A local dry run applies all 30 with no skips and adds no validator problem.

1_armada_dates_old_style.where: L9 content_html x4 (timeline headings), L9 knowledge_checks[4].left x3 (match items), L9 practice_questions[0].marks (model answer; also carries item 2)
1_armada_dates_old_style.detail: 29 July 1588 -> 19 July 1588; 31 July - 4 August -> 21-25 July; 6-7 August -> 27-28 July; 8 August -> 29 July. August-September (journey home) is correct in both calendars and is left alone. Lesson 16 was already Old Style and is unchanged on dates; its Tilbury date of 9 August confirms the Old Style frame.
1_armada_dates_old_style.evidence: Wikipedia 'Spanish Armada' gives the campaign in New Style (sighted off the Lizard 29 July, Plymouth 31 July, Isle of Wight 4 August, Calais 7 August, Gravelines 8 August); Julian is 10 days behind Gregorian in 1588.

2_ships_returned_two_thirds.where: L9 content_html, L9 conclusion_html, L9 knowledge_checks[2].correct (2 -> 1, the 65 option), L9 flashcard_questions[12].a, L9 practice_questions[5].marks, L16 content_html, L16 flashcard_questions[12].q and .a, L16 practice_questions[2].marks
2_ships_returned_two_thirds.detail: 'about 80 of 130' and 'perhaps half' both become about two-thirds, with 'around 65 to 67 of about 130' where a number is needed. Lesson 16 stated the claim negatively ('perhaps half never returned'), so it is turned round to the return side to carry the ruled figure.
2_ships_returned_two_thirds.evidence: Wikipedia 'Spanish Armada' (Aftermath): Garrett Mattingly counts 66 ships back in Spain, with another later; other historians put losses at 44-51 of about 130.

3_essex_ages.where: L13 content_html x3 (body sentence, Privy Council/Cadiz sentence, infographic alt text), L13 knowledge_checks[4].left x3, L13 practice_questions[5].marks
3_essex_ages.detail: Court 17 -> 19, Privy Councillor 26 -> 27, Cadiz 29 -> 30. 'Earl of Essex aged 10' in 1576 is already right on a 1565 birth and is left alone.
3_essex_ages.evidence: Oxford DNB: Robert Devereux born 10 November 1565.

4_1563_poor_relief_act.where: L10 content_html (law timeline), L10 knowledge_checks[4].left[0], L10 practice_questions[1].marks, L10 practice_questions[4].marks
4_1563_poor_relief_act.detail: '1563 Statute of Artificers' becomes '1563 Act for the Relief of the Poor' wherever the claim is that JPs could raise money for poor relief. No wages, apprenticeship or labour passage in the unit names the Statute of Artificers, so nothing was kept under that name.
4_1563_poor_relief_act.evidence: The poor-relief provisions of 1563 are 5 Eliz. I c. 3 (Act for the Relief of the Poor); the Statute of Artificers is 5 Eliz. I c. 4 and covers wages and apprenticeships.

5_parker_37_suspended.where: L7 practice_questions[0].marks ('Parker expelled ministers'), L7 practice_questions[2].marks ('expelling 30 ministers')
5_parker_37_suspended.detail: Both now say he suspended 37 ministers. The lesson 7 body, conclusion and knowledge check already said 37 suspended and are unchanged.
